messages.body_plain:
Hi Antonio,

I want to set search PATH variable on the cluster using backend.parameters(). What is the argument for passing ENV variable in backend.parameters()

Thanks,
Nishant Nagpal

On Monday, May 19, 2014 10:08:38 AM UTC+5:30, Bernardo Hermont wrote:
> Hi folks,
>
> I've been studying some strategy for executing a R code in a hadoop cluster with no R (and also its packages) installed on each Hadoop node of the cluster.
> So, for this Hadoop environment there is no way to have R already previously installed.
>
> So I need to ship all the R and R libs/packages every time I need my R code to be executed.
>
> Does anyone ever had a similar requirement? Any ideas how to implement it?
>
> Bernardo
>
>

backend.parameters is not a function, so I am a confused about the parentheses. Per streaming documentation, you can set env variables with the cmdenv option. That would look like list(hadoop = list(cmdenv="PATH=/some/path/"))

messages.subject: Running RMR scripts via oozie
messages.subject_clean: Running RMR scripts via oozie
messages.body_plain:
Hi All,

We are using oozie shell action to execute our R/RMR scripts in our non secured/kerberized cluster. But this has a problem, in non secured cluster shell action executes the script from user which started tasktracker (which is generally mapred) and not by user who started workflow (as mentioned here - http://blog.cloudera.com/blog/2013/03/how-to-use-oozie-shell-and-java-actions/). This forces us to allow mapred user to edit in our directories which is not very clean solution.

I want know your opinions and experiences with oozie and RMR. Is there any thing like R oozie action exist ?

Thanks
Abhishek

messages.body_plain:
I reintroduced an old bug while eliminating a warning, yikes! Fix in the works. Ultimately, it's a problem with hadoop streaming cmd line and the odd requirement to sort options in a certain way. There are so called generic options that have to go first, and the rest later. If you mix them in the backend.parameter option, you need to preserve this order. If you use both backend.parameters argument to rmr.options and mapreduce, you may end up in trouble as the former's content are put on the cmd line always before the latter. I was hoping over the years streaming would shed this oddity, but it doesn't seem to be happening and a permanent fix would require to embed knowledge of which options are generic and which aren't in rmr2, which is something I am loath to do since it's a permanent coupling with required maintenance and potential for trouble.

Antonio

messages.subject_clean: Unable to run any map-reduce program
messages.body_plain:
It seems you have multiple versions of rmr installed. That function that causes the error changed signature many versions ago. All those package load failures are not necessarily a problem. If you don't need them in the map or reduce function you can ignore the messages or detach the packages before calling mapreduce, if you need them you need to install them on the nodes. But that's not the problem here, the problem is a version mismatch in rmr2.

Antonio

Setup:

I have 2 identical servers running R version 3.1.0
rmr2 is 2.3.0
CDH 4.6

I run the following script:

Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/hadoop-mapreduce/hadoop-streaming-2.0.0-cdh4.6.0.jar")
Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/bin/hadoop")
library(rmr2)
library(rhdfs)
hdfs.init()
ints = to.dfs(1:100)
calc = mapreduce(input = ints, map = function(k, v) cbind(v, 2*v))
Problem:

One server runs fine, I get the results without issue. The other server launches the M/R job but I get the following output in the task logs:

java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat not found
        at org.apache.hadoop.conf.Configuration.getClass(Configuration.java:1806)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.JobConf.getInputFormat(JobConf.java:620)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.runOldMapper(MapTask.java:394)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.run(MapTask.java:332)
        at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child$4.run(Child.java:268)

Observation:
on the "bad" server I see the following two messages I don't see on the "good" server after executing the line
> ints = to.dfs(1:100)
>
> DEPRECATED: Use of this script to execute hdfs command is deprecated.
> Instead use the hdfs command for it.
> Warning message:
> In to.dfs(1:100) : Converting to.dfs argument to keyval with a NULL key
>
> ****I don't think this has anything to do with it but I thought it was worth noting...

Verification Steps:
Verified location of streaming jar and the class was actually in the jar file
Verified Hadoop files are the same on both systems
Verified rmr2/rhdfs packages are the same
Verified environment variables are identical
Verified the /etc/hadoop/conf files are identical too

Any other thoughts on what I can try? I can't re-install CDH here because there are other applications using it happily without issue and I don't want to disturb their configuration.

Please let me know.

Thanks,
Brendan

On Fri, Aug 8, 2014 at 8:12 AM, bayroot22 <bsc...@hotmail.com> wrote:
> Setup:
>
> I have 2 identical servers running R version 3.1.0
> rmr2 is 2.3.0
> CDH 4.6
>
> I run the following script:
>
> Sys.setenv(HADOOP_STREAMING="/opt/cloudera/parcels/CDH/lib/hadoop-mapreduce/hadoop-streaming-2.0.0-cdh4.6.0.jar")
> Sys.setenv(HADOOP_CMD="/usr/bin/hadoop")

> library(rhdfs)
> hdfs.init()
> ints = to.dfs(1:100)
> calc = mapreduce(input = ints, map = function(k, v) cbind(v, 2*v))
> Problem:
>
> One server runs fine, I get the results without issue. The other server launches the M/R job but I get the following output in the task logs:
>
> java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.RuntimeException: java.lang.ClassNotFoundException: Class org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat not found

This must be related to your CLASSPATH. This class is not distributed with R. R issues a command like

hadoop jar streaming.jar -inputformat org.apache.hadoop.streaming.AutoInputFormat ...

That class has to be available to hadoop. I would suggest running one of the hadoop streaming examples that come with hadoop with that option to see what happens, I am pretty sure this is a java problem independent of R. I hate it when support people tell me "not our problem" but we need to count on something and that's hadoop streaming working properly. I don't think it is here.

>         at org.apache.hadoop.conf.Configuration.getClass(Configuration.java:1806)
>         at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.JobConf.getInputFormat(JobConf.java:620)
>         at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.runOldMapper(MapTask.java:394)
>         at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.MapTask.run(MapTask.java:332)
>         at org.apache.hadoop.mapred.Child$4.run(Child.java:268)
>
> Observation:
> on the "bad" server I see the following two messages I don't see on the "good" server after executing the line
> > ints = to.dfs(1:100)
> >
> > DEPRECATED: Use of this script to execute hdfs command is deprecated.
> > Instead use the hdfs command for it.
> > Warning message:
> > In to.dfs(1:100) : Converting to.dfs argument to keyval with a NULL key
> >
> > ****I don't think this has anything to do with it but I thought it was worth noting...
>

What this is saying indirectly is that rmr can not find the hdfs program and therefore has to use hadoop dfs. This points to differences in how hadoop is installed on the two systems or the value of the PATH variable. So you are right it's not related, but it reveals the two systems are not installed identically. Trying to figure out why that difference occurs my help solving the main problem.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:

# This part works:
tmpData <- to.dfs(1:10)

# this part fails
out2 <- mapreduce(
  input = tmpData,
  map = function(k,v) return(keyval(v, v^2)),
  reduce = to.reduce(identity))

# The same code with no reducer does not fail at all:
out1 <- mapreduce(
  input = tmpData,
  map = function(k,v) return(keyval(v, v^2)))

messages.body_plain:
I guess you got 3.2.0 from github. We change the release number as soon as we are done with the previous release, so I wouldn't attach too much meaning to the number in the DESCRIPTION file, unless you download one of the builds from the download page. We increment the third number on master and the second on dev. Then if we want to release a new minor release we merge from dev. Major release is similar. When all features and fixes are done and tests pass in distributed mode, we tag and release. That's how it works. If you just clone master, you get the current commit. Could explode on you. At this point I don't think I am going to delay 3.2.0 but I am sure interested in addressing this problem. It is pretty obvious that I can't repro. So what I'd suggest is that you upgrade to 3.2.0 when we release today and let me know if the problem is solved and we'll take it from there.

Antonio

When you installed rmr2, did it successfully build the hbase classes? Since not many people use them and they have a number of requirements, if anything goes wrong the package build still succeeds and you only get a message. If you overlooked that, than that class wouldn't exist, hence the error. I would go back to the install log or reinstall rmr2 on one node  and look carefully at the console output for the section related to the hbase build. It will start getting ant installed and so forth. This is absolutely unrelated to rhbase.

Antonio

messages.subject: rmr2 3.2.0 and plyrmr 0.4.0
messages.subject_clean: rmr2 3.2.0 and plyrmr 0.4.0
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
we have two new releases, as you may have guessed from the subject. rmr2 3.2.0 is mostly a bugfix release with just one little feature added, which forced us to bump the minor number. plyrmr 0.4.0 introduces fast aggregation by integrating with dplyr a bit more. You may find this evolution a little bit of a work-in-progress but I wanted to get something out to hear from you. The idea is that when you group by a set of columns that defines many small groups, programs become inefficient. dplyr has attacked, if not solved, that problem for the most common aggregations. So we tried to bring into plyrmr some of that goodness with the least amount of overhead. The other improvement is that, like rmr2, plyrmr now has a system of package options and allows multiple backends. Two backends, local and hadoop, are inherited from rmr2. More to come in the future, stay tuned. Feedback and comments welcome as usual. Thanks

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
I think if that line in build_linux.sh read ant-1.9.4 you  wouldn't have gotten that error and you may have completed the build. Strange, our contributor @kahhrut just fixed exactly that point. Either a typo, me botching a merge or something changing in the mirror. This script has been pretty brittle, maybe if we just said: ant > 1.9.2 is a requirement and remove the ant download it would work better. Short term, you could just fix the build script by yourself, or let me do it on monday, in which case you will have to build from the repo, not from a distribution. Whichever works for you. As far as compatibility, we don't have resources to test every combination, you need to grab an additional package, quickcheck, from our Downloads page and run R CMD check path-to-package. If it passes all the tests, that's what we mean by compatibility. They take a long time, because there are many of them, there's latency for each test and there are a few tests at a modest scale. I would love to have more tests at an even larger scale, but it's a trade off. It looks to me you have a fairly recent version of everything and there should be no problem (unfortunately, the tests don't include a test of the hbase IO format to avoid yet-another-dependency for the tests).

Antonio

Okay Antonio no problem . Thanks a lot for your quick & favorable reply. Now, i am going to check the same build with previous versions of Hbase(0.94.x) to make use of rmr package as because recent rmr2 packages are not compatible with Hbase-0.96.x versions. Hope it will work. I will get back to you antonio if i am facing any problem.

Mohan.

> I think if that line in build_linux.sh read ant-1.9.4 you  wouldn't have gotten that error and you may have completed the build. Strange, our contributor @kahhrut just fixed exactly that point. Either a typo, me botching a merge or something changing in the mirror. This script has been pretty brittle, maybe if we just said: ant > 1.9.2 is a requirement and remove the ant download it would work better. Short term, you could just fix the build script by yourself, or let me do it on monday, in which case you will have to build from the repo, not from a distribution. Whichever works for you. As far as compatibility, we don't have resources to test every combination, you need to grab an additional package, quickcheck, from our Downloads page and run R CMD check path-to-package. If it passes all the tests, that's what we mean by compatibility. They take a long time, because there are many of them, there's latency for each test and there are a few tests at a modest scale. I would love to have more tests at an even larger scale, but it's a trade off. It looks to me you have a fairly recent version of everything and there should be no problem (unfortunately, the tests don't include a test of the hbase IO format to avoid yet-another-dependency for the tests).

The problem is that you are testing in your shell and it's not the same environment in which Rscript is called. So executing type -a in your shell doesn't prove anything. The program that's trying to call RScript doesn't run an interactive shell and executes as a different user. This is a problem that came up before, and what works is to install under /usr/bin. messages.subject: Spark
messages.subject_clean: Spark
messages.body_plain:
All,

I would like to get your opinions about how RHadoop and Spark. RHadoop is wonderful, and rmr2/plyrmr are running on top of Hadoop MapReduce.

However, based on what I hear from people in the industry, the next big thing seems to be Spark, and it's going to largely replace Hadoop MapReduce (not Hadoop as a whole, but just the MapReduce part). People often say that Spark is "in-memory," which is not entirely true, since it degrades gracefully if it runs out of memory and thus continues working. So although I have not personally tried Spark (or the SparkR bindings to R), it seems like a pretty cool thing, especially if you have an iterative algorithm. And if you really have non-iterative jobs that have data twenty times your memory, the thing of the future seems to be Apache Tez instead of MapReduce.

So what I've heard (and please correct me if I'm wrong) is that Hadoop MapReduce is going to be replaced mostly by Spark or Tez for new development because there doesn't seem to be a use case where MapReduce is superior any more. (I'm talking about new projects, not existing infrastructure, where MapReduce will continue to be used to continue to support it.)

That leaves me with the question of how RHaddop, which is largely (rmr2/plyrmr) built on top of MapReduce, will fit into the picture going forward.

To be clear, I love RHadoop and I firmly believe that Antonio has done an absolutely superb job integrating Hadoop with R. I'm just curious how this all fits together. I've searched the archives, and there was a brief mentioning of Spark in 2013 here <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/rhadoop/spark/rhadoop/UI8w3HcYeUI/xpI9enF2yv4J> but it was more about Apache Hama. (Not sure whether Hama is taking off as well, but it looks that Spark has far more momentum than Hama right now.)

Thanks,

M

> All,

People often say that Spark is "in-memory," which is not entirely true, since it degrades gracefully if it runs out of memory and thus continues working.

If by degrade gracefully you mean also crashing, I agree.

> So although I have not personally tried Spark (or the SparkR bindings to R), it seems like a pretty cool thing, especially if you have an iterative algorithm. And if you really have non-iterative jobs that have data twenty times your memory, the thing of the future seems to be Apache Tez instead of MapReduce.
> So what I've heard (and please correct me if I'm wrong) is that Hadoop MapReduce is going to be replaced mostly by Spark or Tez for new development because there doesn't seem to be a use case where MapReduce is superior any more. (I'm talking about new projects, not existing infrastructure, where MapReduce will continue to be used to continue to support it.)
>
> That leaves me with the question of how RHaddop, which is largely (rmr2/plyrmr) built on top of MapReduce, will fit into the picture going forward.

Plyrmr can run on top of SparkR, but due to limitations in sparkR I did not announce it and do not support it (I'll make an exception for your bug reports because of your commitment to RHadoop, of course). You clearly are an early adopter, so please take it for a spin, but don't expect a complete implementation. Major omissions: no writing of files (seriously, your computation has to end in memory); no multiple inputs, hence no joins. You can go though the tests and see which ones are skipped in Spark. Slow in some use cases. Work is ongoing for sparkR and I don't want to condemn a project just because it's  in its infancy. We could check out rmr 1.0 and have laugh. But there is a lot of work to do.

>
> > To be clear, I love RHadoop and I firmly believe that Antonio has done an absolutely superb job integrating Hadoop with R

> I'm just curious how this all fits together. I've searched the archives, and there was a brief mentioning of Spark in 2013 here <https://groups.google.com/forum/#!searchin/rhadoop/spark/rhadoop/UI8w3HcYeUI/xpI9enF2yv4J> but it was more about Apache Hama. (Not sure whether Hama is taking off as well, but it looks that Spark has far more momentum than Hama right now.)

In fact there is no Hama backend! Not even unsupported or in a separate branch.

Antonio

> This isn't so much a question as it is a bug report, and recommendation for an easy fix.
>
> I've noticed that when using hb.get.data.frame(), if the columns you specify are not sorted in alphabetical order, then the column headers won't align to the actual data inside the data frame.  This happens because HBase pushes back the column names in alphabetical order, so the column data is aligned by the sorted order of the column names, but the column header assignment uses the initial columns parameter (which may not be sorted).

>             "[[", 3), "[[", cc))))

> g
> ...

messages.body_plain:
write.table is part of the package utils, which is not part of the topics covered here. If you want to use rhbase, the first step is to load rhbase, read the manual, and try one of the functions in the package. I suspect that you are also learning R at the same time ("finding write.table" is an early step for most R users). Trying to learn R and RHadoop at the same time may not be a good idea. Actually, I don't know anyone who's pulled it off. One day, parallel distributed programming may be entry level and we won't program anything else anymore. Today, we are not there.

messages.body_plain:
Hi,
please don't be too concerned if you see posts change status, labels or what not in the next few days. I am trying to experiment with some groups features to better manage your requests. The issue tracker is actually better suited for user support, but many people find forums more familiar or otherwise preferred. Please don't take it personally if you see the "no action needed" flag or if I mark my own answer "best answer", I'd like more diplomatically worded metadata, but that's what the system offers. All these flags are modifiable  by any of the admins whenever the need arises. If I mark a request complete and you have evidence that it is not, not to worry, please reply with the new evidence and I will reopen it, exactly like we do in the issue tracker. I just need some workflow support and some way of directing my focus. Also, when your request becomes a card-carrying bug I am going to open a ticket in the issue tracker, where we can reference code changes, and close the conversation with a link to the issue. To avoid duplications, that thread will become locked to replies. Finally, please refrain from replying to old issues that are just related to your request, again for the sake of workflow management. There is no charge for 1) opening a new thread 2) linking to the old one if you suspect a relation. As usual, feedback is welcome.

Antonio

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using rmr package for a simple "tolower" function to make all the strings lower case. I find that all the content after # sign are gone.
Could you please help me on this? Thank you.

For example if the string file is:
id             doc
1       This is   just a# joke?
2       this **is also a real joke++++++
3       -------we all like this joke very <much>
4       Subject: TM# 123456

## The code is: ===========
clean.map = function(k,v){
  doc_low <- tolower(v$doc)
  keyval(v$id,doc_low)
}
column.names <- c("id", "doc")
clean.dirIn<- 'docs'
docs.input.format = make.input.format("csv", sep="\t", row.names=NULL, col.names=column.names)
cleanMap_out <- from.dfs(mapreduce(input=clean.dirIn,
                                   input.format = docs.input.format,
                                   map=clean.map))
##==========
The result is:
> cleanMap_out
$key
 [1]  1  2  3  4

$val
 [1] "this is   just a"
 [2] "this **is also a real joke++++++"
 [3] "-------we all like this joke very <much>"
 [4] "subject: tm"

Thanks,
Jingran
